title: Install and recover Cast program releases
summary: Understand matching program and documentation packaging, owned selectors, frontend credential loading, deployment setup, and verified program recovery without replacing discovery state.
use_when: Cast program packaging, selector ownership, installation compatibility or verified program recovery must be understood.
The installed frontend's environment and credential loading or Cell deployment setup must be understood.
do_not_use_when: Collection or downstream application work should be started.
The requested result is provider billing, credential replacement, destructive state reset or a schedule.
outcome: One matching verified program/documentation selection with separate discovery-state compatibility and recovery boundaries.
effects: Installation stages content-addressed payload, static frontend, Rust installer and exact provider bundle and advances only Cast-owned selectors.
Program selection creates no discovery database, live-state migration, schedule or provider request.
The frontend executes user-owned shell configuration for provider keys; Cell configuration separately initializes missing state and optionally applies a complete config file.
authority: Cast owns release identity, integrity verification, installation and matching command/provider selectors.
Discovery state retains its own lifecycle; user shell configuration and remote provider readiness remain separately owned.
success: Installation or recovery selects a verified matching program and provider bundle, confirmed through command identity and help checks.
failure_and_recovery: Foreign selectors and mismatched candidate/provider versions are refused. A failed switch restores prior selectors.
Recover only a verified canonical owned release through a trusted tested installer. Program recovery leaves discovery state and budgets unchanged.
Remove a stale .update-lock only after proving no Cast deployer is running; never remove another active writer's lock.
privacy: Provider keys do not enter arguments, saved config, provider contracts or output. The user owns executable .zshrc behavior.
CLI usage records command identity, time and thread ID without arguments, output or outcomes; recording errors preserve product results.
does_not_authorize: A collection run, schedule, provider purchase, credential replacement, state deletion or downstream application workflow.

consumers.statement: The current user may install or recover Cast programs through a trusted tested candidate, inspect selectors and understand wrapper credential loading.

preconditions.statement: Installation requires a validated executable candidate matching the provider release, user-owned paths and supported macOS shell tools. Recovery requires a verified retained canonical owned release. Chancery need not be installed for Cast to operate.

inputs.statement: install accepts absolute --binary and --bundle paths, optional --home PATH and --expected-current absent|releases/HASH. recover accepts --release ABSOLUTE_RELEASE_DIRECTORY.

Cell deployment setup accepts optional absolute state_dir and config_file paths after program selection. A supplied complete config_file is applied through config set; omitted settings remain unchanged.
The frontend reads THEIRSTACK_API_KEY and BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY from user-owned ~/.zshrc. It preserves state selection and command-usage values captured before shell configuration.

outputs.statement: Installed ~/.local/bin/cast, ~/.local/bin/cast-install and Cast's provider selector follow one atomic current release. Command identity and help establish program selection, not current provider readiness.

data_semantics.statement: Release integrity verifies installed program/documentation artifacts. Discovery records, provider authentication and external collection have separate success conditions.

identity_and_units.statement: Release HASH identifies exact payload, frontend, Rust installer and provider bytes beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Cast/install/releases/HASH. The cell-install-v2 manifest is manifest.json; package/install retains the Rust installer.
Program installation defines no provider billing unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Program checks observe the selected release. Catalog publication, command versions and local readiness do not establish current remote-provider balance, authentication or collection success.
Artifact integrity and selected release identity are local installation observations; discovery freshness belongs to retained record evidence.

access.statement: The installed frontend suppresses trace and output while sourcing ~/.zshrc. It passes HOME, fixed system PATH, optional CAST_STATE_DIR, provider keys, CODEX_THREAD_ID, CHANCERY_USAGE_DB, CHANCERY_USAGE_DISABLED and CHANCERY_USAGE_INTERNAL. It preserves arguments and stdin. Help, version and --register-usage bypass shell configuration.
User-owned shell commands and side effects remain the user's responsibility; Chancery does not execute or validate that configuration.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Deployment takes product and catalog writer locks, refuses foreign selectors, verifies candidate/provider versions, switches current atomically and restores prior selectors after a failed switch.
Prior releases remain available. Recovery verifies retained legacy or cell-install-v2 artifacts before selection and does not restore discovery state, configuration or consumed budgets.
Cell configure invokes cast init without collection and optionally replaces complete config. It preserves existing records and consumed budgets and creates no collection schedule.
An abruptly killed deployer can leave .update-lock. Runtime mutation uses a separate kernel-backed lock.

operational_limits.statement: Installation creates no database, daemon, LaunchAgent, scheduler binding, provider request, model job or automatic live-state migration.
No installation-latency objective, future migration promise, automatic state rollback or deprecation window is defined.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Provider release, contract version, installation format and database/config/export schemas evolve separately. The exact provider bundle is published and recovered with its matching product release; Chancery is documentation, not a runtime requirement.

Register declared inventory with cast --register-usage after installation or update. CLI usage recording requires nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID; private records contain identity, time and thread ID only. Internal product calls are excluded and recording errors preserve command results.

reliances.statement: Program recovery must verify compatibility with selected discovery state and configuration without restoring them.
Installed credential loading relies on user-owned ~/.zshrc executed by zsh; no dedicated installed contract covers that executable configuration.
